CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Fetal tissue
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal tissue analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
Complementary QF-PCR Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH: Oligonucleotide array analysis was performed using the GenomeScan 8000 platform containing approximately 60,000 probes with a median resolution of 120kb. DNA was extracted from fetal tissue and processed according to standard protocols. Test and reference DNA samples were differentially labeled and co-hybridized to the array. Data analysis was performed using GenomeView software. All positional information is based on the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

QF-PCR: Quantitative fluorescence polymerase chain reaction was performed for rapid aneuploidy detection of chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y using polymorphic STR markers.

RESULTS

Array CGH Result: arr(1-22)x2,(X,Y)x1
Interpretation: Normal male chromosome complement

No copy number imbalances detected above the resolution of this array.

QF-PCR Result: No evidence of triploidy detected
All tested chromosomes showed normal disomic patterns consistent with male karyotype.

SUMMARY
Array CGH analysis reveals a normal male chromosome complement with no detectable copy number abnormalities. The QF-PCR analysis confirms normal copy number for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y with no evidence of triploidy.

LIMITATIONS
This array has a median resolution of 120kb and is designed to detect genomic imbalances greater than 3Mb with high confidence. Smaller copy number variants, balanced rearrangements, low-level mosaicism (<20%), and point mutations cannot be detected by this methodology. Uniparental disomy and methylation abnormalities are also not detectable by array CGH.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required for this sample based on current findings.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
